title: What engine is beste to work with caude/mcp?
author: salombs
selftext:
Unity, Godot or Unreal? 

For automation

comments.author: frankenstein-0x00e
comments.body:
Godot is goated tbh

  
and AI (claude) is so good at it   
it doesnt even need MCP it just rawdogs it, it can run specific parts of the game (scenes) to do individual tests (for me grapping objects, or testing smoke effects etc)

and it can run it headless, record gameplay, script gameplay, test, its crazy



It also supports Rust integration (thru plugin) so you can double your FPS when you are optimizing your game lol

replies.author: MrNotmark
replies.body:
I highly doubt rust doubles FPS, the programming language doesn't really matter unless you're doing something very simple I would say, even gdscript is good because it talks with the engine directly.

Most of the fps comes from the draw calls and objects on the screen, lighting etc. That's all GPU. 
Cpu wise the only thing you should do is send draw calls and work on physics and those can be just as fast in C# as in rust I would say

maybe if you write your procedural logics in scripts that would be better in C# or rust compared to gdscript, but come on, the biggest bottleneck in most game is always the API calls and you calling engine methods

comments.author: random_boss
comments.body:
I use Unity but was getting frustrated at some limitations so did an advisory session on switching. Ultimately ended up sticking with Unity. 

The main call Claude had against unreal is that its files are stored as binary whereas unity is stored as text, making it harder 
for agents to reason over and costs more tokens. The second was that Unreal (currently) requires an MCP whereas Unity offers a CLI.

The main value for Godot traditionally is that people like using its editor, but if you’re doing AI development you’re not using the editor, so at that point its just a worse Unity. The second thing people like about Godot is that it’s completely free, which is absurd because unreal and unity are both free unless you make a certain amount of money…which really means they’re all just free. 

So I stuck with unity (and am grinding through the problems that made me want to switch)

replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body:
Uunless you REALLY know what you're doing - and you're here, so you probably don't - do not try to have fckn ChatGPT or Claude build you an engine

you could get a quarter of the way into your project with your 'custom engine lol' and then realize it has a massive memory leak issue or doesn't cache properly or does any number of other catastrophic under-the-hood things that you'd never realize it is doing until it is too late. and these are all solved problems that you have re-introduced for yourself and now need to try and fix, but the standard tools for doing so are tucked inside of libraries that your 'custom engine lol' can't load

comments.author: NeonCenturionSPQR
comments.body:
Godot. 

It's literally structural. 

Claude Opus 5.5 is well trained on the current Godot syntax. Everything in Godot is stored as flat text. Down to the scenes, project settings, properties, everything. So if I'm being honest, you can develop massive, massive games without ever touching an mcp.

replies.author: salombs
replies.body: Fable is good for Godot? Im thinking to use fable for animation 3d, what you think?

replies.author: NeonCenturionSPQR
replies.body:
I ran some tests with Godot, just giving it asset packs, and a large, specific prompt, alongside a Claude code plugin I made, to take it from nothing to a polished, alpha or beta level. Ran until finished, again with the plugin, and absolutely spectacular results. To walk away and come back to something with little to no bugs whatsoever. 

I'll see if I can public up one or two of the repositories tonight just as examples for you to see what is ultimately possible.

But yes other engines can't just "be read" by ai, necessitating the use of an MCP to do more than programing. In Godot, the AI can wholesale modify EVERY ASPECT OF YOUR GAME.
